title: CERT-In reports unauthorised transactions at financial and government-linked payment service providers
date_note: Reuters (via ThePrint, 21 November) and The420.in say the advisory was issued on Friday; The420.in gives 20 November. The CERT-In advisory itself was not read.
place: New Delhi, India (agency location; victims not named)
summary: According to Reuters, relayed by ThePrint, CERT-In said in an advisory on Friday that it had reported unauthorised transactions at service providers for banking and financial entities and at technology providers supporting government-linked payments. It said attackers altered business records or approval relationships, then used legitimate payment processes. Reuters says CERT-In did not say how much was paid out or by whom.
plain: India's cyber agency says fraudulent payments were made through service providers by changing business records or approvals. Amounts and victims were not given.
exec: Payment fraud via suppliers and payout platforms is reported by India's national CERT; no amounts or victims were disclosed.
action: Government bodies, non-financial payout platforms and technology service providers: read the CERT-In advisory recommendations; the pages read do not list them.

validation.note: ThePrint is Reuters copy and The420.in relays the same account; not independent. CERT-In advisory not read or linked by either. Business Standard and The Hawk answered 403.
